hypotheses.statement: The incident was caused by an expired TLS certificate on payments-gateway.internal, which prevented the checkout-api payments-connector from establishing secure connections, leading to upstream_unavailable errors and 502 responses on POST /v2/checkout/submit.

observed_facts.statement: Release 2026.5.14-a deployed to production at 09:09:52Z. Changes: copy edits to three checkout confirmation email templates, and a dependency bump of the CSV export library used by the nightly reconciliation job. No code path in this release is reachable from POST /v2/checkout/submit.

checkout-api payments-connector: repeated outbound TLS handshake failures to payments-gateway.internal:8443. Error: certificate verify failed: certificate has expired. First occurrence 09:11:47Z, sustained at 40-60 events per second.
checkout-api: POST /v2/checkout/submit returning 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted 3 retries. Correlated with payments-connector TLS failures.
Alert checkout-api-error-ratio fired. Observed 5xx ratio 0.184 over a 5 minute window against an objective of 0.005. Affected route: POST /v2/checkout/submit. Alert remained firing until 09:58:10Z.
Alert checkout-api-latency fired. p99 latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit rose from 240ms to 10400ms. The 10400ms value sits at the configured client timeout.
INC-7742 opened at 09:15:00Z, severity 1, title 'Checkout submit failing for all customers'. Impact field left empty. No customer-impact estimate was recorded.

Trace 5f21c0: POST /v2/checkout/submit total 10402ms. Span checkout.validate 12ms ok. Span payments.authorize 10388ms error, terminated by client timeout, no upstream response recorded. No span entered the email template or CSV export code paths.
checkout-api payments-connector: outbound TLS handshakes to payments-gateway.internal:8443 succeeding again. Error rate returned to baseline at 09:57:55Z.

Responder C from the payments-gateway team: 'Our leaf certificate for payments-gateway.internal expired at 09:11:40Z. We rotated it and it took effect at 09:57:50Z. We have no record of who owns the renewal automation for that host.'
Rollback of checkout-api to 2026.5.13-c completed at 10:04:18Z. The 5xx ratio had already returned to 0.004 at 09:58:10Z, six minutes before this rollback completed.
INC-7742 marked resolved. Resolution note reads only 'rolled back and recovered'. The note does not mention the certificate rotation reported in the incident channel.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or runbook identifying the owner of the renewal automation for the payments-gateway.internal certificate.
open_questions.question: Who is responsible for the automated renewal of the payments-gateway.internal TLS certificate?

open_questions.missing_evidence: A post-incident review or impact assessment quantifying affected customers, transactions, or revenue.
open_questions.question: What was the actual customer and business impact of the incident?

summary: The checkout-5xx incident was caused by an expired TLS certificate on the payments-gateway.internal service, which began failing at 09:11:47Z. This prevented the checkout-api payments-connector from establishing secure connections, resulting in 502 upstream_unavailable errors and high latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit requests. The system recovered after the certificate was rotated at 09:57:50Z. A coincidental, unrelated deployment occurred minutes before the failure, leading to initial misattribution, but logs, traces, and team communication confirm the certificate expiration as the root cause.

timeline.statement: payments-connector TLS handshake failures begin due to an expired certificate on payments-gateway.internal.
payments-connector TLS handshakes succeed again; error rate returns to baseline.
Payments-gateway team reports certificate expired at 09:11:40Z and was rotated, taking effect at 09:57:50Z.
Rollback of checkout-api to 2026.5.13-c completed (after recovery).
INC-7742 marked resolved with incomplete resolution note.
